classes.name: BasisEnv
classes.docu:
BasisEnv

The BasisEnv class retrieves the environment variables from the current
environment for an application.  The environment variables are retrieved
using the "set" command on Windows and the "env" command on Unix.  The
output from these command has the following format:

   =

The pairs are split and stored.  The BasisEnv.getProperty() method is
used to retrieved a specific value for the specified key.

The load() method has been added to generate the appropriate command
(given the OS) and parse the output.  On Windows, the command is

    cmd /C set  (for NT)  or  command.com /C set (for 98/95)

while on Unix the command looks like

    /usr/bin/env  (but may be /bin/env)

If the first command throws an exception, other additional commands will be
tried.  This is more useful under Unix where the location of the env command
varies (sometimes in /bin, maybe in /usr/bin, etc).

Once run, the output from the command is fed into the method 
load(InputStream).  The load(InputStream) method has been overridden to
expect data in the format "=", one pair per line.  If the
load(InputStream) method is invoked outside this class's constructor, the
data must be in the same format.

classes.name: ThreadGroupLocal
classes.docu:
Class to store and retrieve variables specific to individual thread
groups.

The initial requirement for this class was to insure that only the first
SysWindow created in a thread group would display a menu bar.  See
com.basis.bbj.client.console.SysWinMenuBar for this particular example of
using the ThreadGroupLocal class.

After a ThreadGroup only has daemon threads inside of it, all of its
copies of ThreadLocal variables are subject to garbage collection
(unless other references to these copies exist).

Be careful using ThreadGroupLocal from Daemon threads since daemon
threads will not keep a value active by themselves.

SplashScreen constructor.

Parameters:

  • p_imageURL is the URL of the image to use for the splash window. It should be a path starting at /com/...
  • p_secs is the number of seconds the splash window should stay up.

startTimer
starts the Timer, causing it to send actionPerformed()
